questions.q: What makes a transaction log backup fundamentally different from a full or differential backup, not just smaller?
options: It's a record of every transaction in order since the last log backup, not a snapshot of data pages
It only backs up the database schema, never actual row data
It's taken manually by the DBA while full and differential are always automatic
It can only be restored on SQL Server running on an Azure VM
questions.explain: Full and differential backups are both data-page snapshots; a log backup is a record of transactions in order, which is what makes point-in-time recovery possible.

questions.q: Why does the log backup chain specifically make point-in-time recovery possible, when full and differential backups alone cannot?
options: Replaying transactions in order lets you stop at any exact second, not just at the moment a full or differential backup happened to run
Log backups are stored in a different, faster storage tier than full backups
Log backups automatically delete corrupted transactions before restore
Full and differential backups cannot be restored together under any circumstances
questions.explain: Restoring only full and differential backups can only put you back at one of the moments they ran; replaying the transaction log on top lets you stop at any point in between.

questions.q: How often does Azure SQL Database automatically take transaction log backups?
options: Every 5-10 minutes, continuously
Once per day, overnight
Only when the DBA manually triggers BACKUP LOG
Every 12-24 hours, alongside the differential
questions.explain: Azure's automatic log backup cadence is every 5-10 minutes — tighter than the 15-minute interval Lesson 2 planned by hand for an on-prem-style schedule.

questions.q: Why is a 5-10 minute backup cadence practical for log backups but would be wasteful for full backups at the same frequency?
options: A log backup is small because it's transaction records, not full data pages, so frequent runs are cheap
Log backups skip the Billing table to save time
Azure compresses log backups more aggressively than full backups
Full backups are actually taken every 5-10 minutes too, just not shown to the DBA
questions.explain: Because a log backup only contains transaction records rather than copying entire data pages, running it frequently is cheap — unlike a full backup, which copies everything every time.

questions.q: For Overlook's healthcare scheduling and billing database, why does 'restore to 2:35pm, one minute before the bad script ran' matter more than 'restore to last night's backup'?
options: Restoring only to last night could lose a full day of real appointments and payments, which point-in-time restore avoids
Azure SQL Database cannot restore to last night's backup under any circumstances
Patient data is legally required to be restored only to the exact second of an incident
Differential backups make nightly restores technically impossible
questions.explain: For a database with real daily activity, restoring only to the last full or differential backup risks losing significant real data — the log backup chain is what makes a much more precise, much less lossy restore possible.
